title: skyBlip device status (v1)
description: The answer to {"cmd":"status"} on the config endpoint, and the one frame the device also sends without being asked: while a link is up, a charging flip, a change of power level or a five-percent step of the state of charge pushes it to every subscribed central. One flat object in one notification, sized against the 182-byte payload the narrowest phone in the field carries with every key at its widest (154 bytes, pinned byte for byte in firmware/test/products/test_comms_report.cpp). It carries what a pilot's screen shows and nothing a bench reads: why the device came up is 'reset' and whether a gauge is fitted is 'valid' in diagnostics.v1, the address and the callsign are config.v1's. A key with no reading behind it is ABSENT, never a zero. Keys arrive in the order listed here, which scripts/check_status_schema.py holds the firmware to (firmware/core/comms/config_reports.cpp). The producer (firmware) owns this schema; consumers pin a version.

flight.description: The confirmed flight state. Every settings change and upload is refused unless this reads ground, so 'unknown' refuses too

upload.description: A firmware upload window is open: granted by the confirmation gesture on the device, true only on the ground, closed for good by a takeoff

battery_percent.description: State of charge, 0 where the device takes itself down rather than where a datasheet calls the cell empty, read on the charging curve while the charger holds the rail. ABSENT until the gauge has a sample, and for ever on a board with no divider

charging.description: The charger is holding the rail

power_level.description: What core/power's cutoff rule made of the same samples. LOW refuses every durable write but the flight record, CUTOFF is the device taking itself down. '--' is Unknown: no believable reading yet

went_dark_flat.description: The last time this unit went dark it was for a flat cell: the cutoff took it down, or a switch-on was refused below the boot lockout. The glass says FLAT BATTERY until a charger wakes the unit, and this outlives that frame: true for the whole of the one boot that followed, false from the boot after. The self-test page prints the same fact as WAS FLAT

die_temp_c.description: Die temperature in whole degrees Celsius, rounded away from zero. ABSENT rather than zero when no reading younger than 30 seconds exists, because 0.0 C is a plausible hangar morning. Same key and same value as diagnostics.v1's
